Q: How to convert query results into dict using Python? A:

This method is the cleanest because it handles the mapping at the driver level

import psycopg2
from psycopg2.extras import RealDictCursor

# establishing the connection
conn = psycopg2.connect(
    database="CONNETpy",
    user='postgres',
    password='pass',
    host='localhost',
    port='5432'
)

# Use RealDictCursor to get results as dictionaries
cursor = conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor)

tables = ["Class_A", "Class_B", "Class_C"]
combined_dict = {}

for table in tables:
    cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}")
    # fetchall() returns a list of RealDict objects
    results = cursor.fetchall()
    # Store results in the master dict using the table name as the key
    combined_dict[table] = [dict(row) for row in results]

print(combined_dict)

cursor.close()
conn.close()

If you can't change the cursor type, you have to manually pair the cursor.description with the row (same as the answer by Pravash):

combined_dict = {}
for table in tables:
    cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}")
    column_names = [desc[0] for desc in cursor.description]
    results = cursor.fetchall()
    combined_dict[table] = [dict(zip(column_names, result)) for result in results]

cursor.close()
conn.close()

Q: Environment detection: node.js or browser A:

Testing for browser environment vs Node.js

Testing for a browser environment is as simple as testing for a falsy document.all object:

// Evaluates to true in modern web browsers including IE
var is_browser = typeof document=='object' && !Object(document && document.all) || /*@cc_on!@*/false;

In the above, Object() either returns a truthy object since all objects are truthy, or in browsers, Object() returns a falsy document.all object as per the HTML5 spec. See: Why is document.all falsy?

It all started in the '00s when popular browsers wanted to support IE's non-standard document.all without triggering IE-specific code and were already putting such measures into place. Falsy document.all was soon written into the HTML5 spec and is long since supported in every modern browser including Internet Explorer 11.

The /*@cc_on!@*/false tacked on at the end is an IE-only feature that evaluates to true and is needed to make it work in IE 10 and below.

The beauty of this approach is that it can't be spoofed since falsy objects are not possible under Node.js. Caveat: absence of document.all might also mean code is running in a worker that doesn't have access to the DOM.

Q: How to set GRADLE_USER_HOME in VSCode? A:

vscode-java extension has a setting called java.import.gradle.user.home. Use this setting to set the GRADLE_USER_HOME. If u are using latest version of vscode-gradle, it also share the same setting.

At current time of writing, do note that java.import.gradle.user.home must be absolute value and does not support variable expansion.

Q: Error Desc: Exception from HRESULT: 0x800A0046 (CTL_E_PERMISSIONDENIED) A:

Without more information about what your file system is like, what permissions you have, and what exactly are you trying to do and use in your program, there is little to no way of knowing how to help you.

However, I've encountered this problem in the past due to legacy DLLs mixed in with more recent technologies - such as .Net 1 vs .Net 4.5.

Old DLLs under .Net 4.5 and above are a pain in the backside to manage and make sure they run properly. They cause memory leaks, they don't respect memory properly and they are hardcoded in many ways to do things that .Net 4.5 and above would do better these days.

I suggest you provide us with your project settings, and your COM references, because one of them is most likely the reason you're getting this error.

It's a process of elimination. Eliminate one Reference at a time, comment out code, debug, etc until you find the culprit DLL that gives you the problem. AND THEN you need to decide whether to use another DLL, another Reference or better yet, do without that offending DLL in the first place.

Good luck,
